tender.title: Rough Sleeping Services to include Migrant Accommodation Pathway Services, Crisis Prevention and Response Services and London Navigator Team Services
tender.description:
Transport for London is procuring on behalf of the Greater London Authority (GLA).  The Mayor's Rough Sleeping Plan of Action sets out the bold vision to end rough sleeping in London by 2030. The services commissioned through this process will play a key role in achieving this ambition, through preventing homelessness and providing specialist support to those who are sleeping rough.
This procurement covers the delivery of three lots which are listed below:
Lot 1 - Migrant Accommodation Pathways Service (MAPS)
This is a specialist service aimed at improving outcomes for non-UK nationals rough sleeping or at risk of rough sleeping in London. It will replace the current MAPS service, which includes the Roma Rough Sleeping Team and the Link Worker Team. The service will include the following elements:
A dedicated migrant homelessness advice function through second‑tier professional support and direct advice to service users;
An assessment and case resolution function for those facing additional barriers to resolving their homelessness, including international reconnections;
Access to independent legal advice;
Specialist support for Roma people rough sleeping or at risk of rough sleeping;
Emergency accommodation provision to facilitate assessing or securing routes out of homelessness for homeless migrants;
A system capacity building and coordination function.
General Optional Services: 
Provision of additional staffing
Provision of additional accommodation
Additional client costs
Initial Term of 3 years with 3 optional years - 3+1+1+1. Contract value for the full 6 years is up to £13.7M. An allowance of up to 50% is included for enacting the optional services, with a maximum possible contract value for the service of up to £20.5M.
Lot 2 - Crisis Prevention and Response Service (CPRS)
This is a new service which will replace the current Rapid Response Outreach Team. It will also incorporate the phoneline, currently delivered through the separate StreetLink London service.
To enable a transition from current service provision to a new model of support focused on prevention and assisting more people without the need for outreach contact, there is a phased approach to the delivery of the service.
Throughout the contract, the service will include:
A pan-London, self-referral phoneline service taking calls from people sleeping rough or at imminent risk of sleeping rough.
An outreach response on the night transport network.
Assessment, triage, advice, guidance and one-off advocacy.
In the first year of the contract, the service will also deliver an outreach response to all StreetLink alerts in 26 boroughs.
In Year 2, the service will transition away from this outreach-led approach and will then include:
A community team providing in-person support across a range of settings
Short-term casework for those who require it
General Optional Services: 
Expansion of the capacity of the phoneline
Expansion of the night transport function
Provision of additional staffing
Initial Term of 3 years with 3 optional years - 3+1+1+1. Contract value for the full 6 years is up to £14.4M. An allowance of up to 50% is included for enacting the optional services, with a maximum possible contract value for the service of up to £21.6M.
Lot 3 - London Navigator Team (LNT)
The service provides specialist support for people with long histories of rough sleeping, who are part of the Target Priority Group. It includes:
Personalised and intensive support which can stay with people on their journey from the streets to home.
Support for people experiencing severe and multiple disadvantage to navigate local systems to access both housing and the support they need in all areas of their life.
The LNT Housing Scheme - 40 ringfenced social housing units, housing people from the LNT caseload under a housing-led model.
General Optional Services:
Supporting any additional properties added to the LNT Housing Scheme
Expanding the LNT through the provision of additional staffing
Service user costs for any additional cases added to the LNT caseload, above the number which the provider has modelled for in the core service
Initial Term of 3 years with 3 optional years - 3+1+1+1. Contract value for the full 6 years is up to £9.4M. An allowance of up to 50% is included for enacting the optional services, with a maximum possible contract value for the service of up to £14.2M.
The above values include core services and general optional services for each of the three Lots. Contract duration will be for three (3) years and options to extend the contract for a further period of up to three (3) years, exercisable in one or more periods to a maximum of three (3) years. The maximum duration of the contract (including all extensions) will be no more than six (6) years. 
Total Value (estimated) - £56,374,308 (full 6‑year maximum value including extensions and optional services). This value is across all three services.
Contract dates (Estimated)- 3 years initial + up to 3 optional extension years
Bidders may apply for multiple lots, however, awards will be limited to up to 50% of the bidder's annual turnover. This controls delivery risk, avoids overreliance on single providers and protects market diversity. 
Each lot includes core and optional services.

tender.description:
Westminster City Council (WCC) are recommissioning Housing First Services in two Lots:
-	Lot 1 Housing First Support Service
-	Lot 2 Housing First Violence Against Women and Girl (VAWG)
The service is a pivotal and strategically aligned provision at the 
heart of the WCC’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping Strategy 2024. 
This service is a cornerstone of our ambition to prevent 
homelessness, enhance recovery, and transform lives through a 
dynamic, tailored, and outcomes-driven approach.
Housing First is a widely renowned homelessness intervention strategy that prioritises providing permanent housing with high quality wraparound support. Its aims are for service users to retain their tenancies and graduate from intensive floating support to independence, therefore ending recurrent cycles of homelessness. 
Housing First has been an established commissioned service in Westminster since 2017. This procurement aims to continue delivering this service primarily for clients who are currently in social tenancies through Housing First and to allow flexibility to accommodate new service users where new tenancies become available.  
The overarching aim of this tender is to commission an intensive floating support model for Housing First, structured into two distinct lots: one providing a specialist service for women affected by Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) to support up to 36 women, and the other delivering a generic Housing First mixed gender service supporting up to 48 service users. 
The estimated Service Commencement Date is 1 June 2026. The Initial 
Contract Period is 3 years, with provision for extension, at WCC’s discretion, for up to a further 3 years (1+1+1 years), providing a total contract period of up to 6 years (calculated from the Service Commencement Date), expiring no later than 31 May 2032.
During the Contract Period the Authority may, at its sole discretion, require additional Services to be delivered by the Provider, i.e. should additional tenancies or funding opportunities become available, in excess of the existing Services Users, the Provider will liaise with the Authority to agree provisions. Any increase will be subject to funding availability and to the Authority’s governance procedures.  Any agreed scale-up of the Service would be aligned to Housing First model e.g. one extra worker per five to seven Service Users plus management support consideration. During the contract period the service may be scaled up to support an additional 10 -14 Service Users, this is subject to clause 47 of the Contract and is at the Authorities’ discretion. The budget published does not include this additional capacity.

tender.description:
Contract Background
The contract is for single supplier for the provision of Chillers, Air Conditioning Systems and Refrigeration Maintenance Contract at The Pirbright Institute.
Scope of works
Work Package 1 – Chillers, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration Equipment 
This works package is for a single supplier to service and or repair all refrigeration, air conditioning and associated systems at The Pirbright Institute.
Service visits should be arranged according to F gas regulations, site requirements and insurance inspections schedules. 
The attached schedule (Schedule 5.C - Refrigeration Plant List) details the buildings, the details of the Chillers, Freezers and Air conditioning equipment and frequency of service visits required. A site plan showing the locations and relative sizes of these buildings is included in Schedule 5.D - Site Plan.
The contractor will be expected to advise on the condition of the equipment and provide details of any remedial works required following each service. Critical remedial works should be advised to Pirbright on the same day.
Quotations for non-critical remedial works should be provided to Pirbright within 1 week of a service visit.
The contractor should also allow for the supply of:
•	1 x vacuum pump
•	1 x recovery machine
•	1 x set of gauges
•	1 x refrigerant leak detector
These will be kept in our restricted areas and will only be used by the contractor.  These can be taken out of containment and returned to contractor at the end of the contract. This is to prevent the unnecessary passage and time-consuming decontamination for contractor’s tools when work is being done on our contained systems. 
Within the first 6 months of the contract the contractor will be expected to provide a critical spares list and an itemised quotation for all systems.
Service reports should be left on site or received by site on the day of the service and test certificates should be received by site within one week of the service visit.
In addition to providing their own access equipment, it is expected that the supplier will include in their works, performing basic tasks required to access equipment such as lifting ceiling panels.
Work Package 2 – Emergency Call out Service
The supplier of works package 1 must also provide a 24-hour emergency call out service. With an engineer site attendance time of under 4 hours. All specification requirements that are associated with work package 1 also apply this work package.
Work Package 3 – Insurance Inspection Facilitation
The contractor will need to allow for the supply of an engineer to aid our insurance inspector with PSSR inspections on chillers. This can take up to 5 days per year.

tender.title: Strengthening the Global Trading System (GTS)​ ​ ​
tender.description:
The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) is undertaking Early Market Engagement (EME) in advance of a potential future procurement opportunity for Strengthening the Global Trading System (GTS).
The GTS contract is expected to form part of the Trade Centre of Expertise (Trade CoE), which sits within FCDO's wider Growth Community of Expertise (Growth CoE). The Trade CoE provides technical assistance to help developing countries participate more effectively in international trade and support inclusive, sustainable and export-led economic growth.
The proposed GTS support offer will focus on strengthening the capacity of developing countries, including Least Developed Countries (LDCs), to engage in, influence and benefit from the multilateral trading system, particularly through the World Trade Organization (WTO).
Indicative areas of support may include:
- Technical assistance and advisory services to strengthen developing country participation in international trade negotiations and trade related processes.
- Capacity building and institutional support to improve engagement with the WTO and other relevant multilateral and regional trade bodies.
- Policy, legal and technical assistance to support the implementation of, and access to benefits from, international trade agreements.
- Research, analysis and knowledge sharing to strengthen trade policy development and decision making.
FCDO welcomes engagement from organisations with relevant expertise in trade and development, including SMEs and consortia.
Suppliers interested in this opportunity, whether as a potential Prime Contractor or subcontractor, are invited to attend (virtually) an Early Market Engagement Event on Thursday 10 September at 10:00am (UK time). The session will provide further information on the emerging requirement and offer suppliers an opportunity to contribute views that will help inform FCDO's approach.
Please note that the information provided at this stage is indicative only and does not constitute a commitment to procure. The final scope, requirements and contractual arrangements will be confirmed in any future Tender Notice.
The route to market has not yet been determined. Feedback received through FCDO's preliminary market engagement activities will be used to help shape the procurement strategy and inform decisions on the most appropriate delivery model.

tender.description:
Nexus are looking for a design and build contract to  undertake  the improvement of existing facilities at South Gosforth Control Centre for staff to create a fit for purpose working environment.
The aim of the project is to improve the existing facilities at South Gosforth Control Centre for staff to create a fit for purpose working environment. The building was constructed in 1980 and has undergone limited refurbishment in 2014 and 2021/22. There is a requirement for a more flexible working environment and improved welfare facilities from users to align with Nexus Places principles. However, following investigations of the structure and its systems several assets require renewal or upgrades to achieve compliance, including security measures. The Control Centre must remain operational 24/7 during the project.
We are looking for a contractor to undertake the design and build contract for the refurbishment of the Control Centre.
Scope requirements

Accessibility improvements for movements to and around the building (not including the provision of a lift)
Traffic management and street furniture improvements
Roof and roof safe access improvements
Drainage system improvements
Fire detection and protection improvements
Lighting, high voltage and low voltage systems upgrades
Ventilation and gas suppression system upgrades
M&E provisions for upgrades to welfare facilities
Security system upgrades (inc. CCTV)
Removal of internal walls and installation of glass partitions and soundproofed internal walls
Improvements to canteen and welfare facilities
Provision for additional meeting rooms, breakout areas and desks
Improvements to ICT systems and provisions for user usage
A supplier is required to carry out a design and build contract for the refurbishment of the Control Centre.
The Control Centre must remain operational 24/7 during the project.

tender.title: Best Start Family Hubs
tender.description:
The national Best Start Family Hubs and Healthy Babies programme sets a refreshed direction for family and health support from April 2026 to March 2029. It builds on the learning from Sure Start, Family Hubs and Start for Life, with a clear expectation that local areas bring together health, education, early years, parenting and community support so that families can access help earlier, more easily and in places they already know and trust.
The programme places strong emphasis on early identification, prevention and reducing inequalities, particularly during pregnancy and the early years when the foundations for lifelong health, learning and development are laid. Best Start Family Hubs should provide a welcoming and inclusive front door for families, supported by a wider network of linked local services and outreach locations, so that families can receive the right support at the right time and are not left to navigate services on their own.
The updated national guidance describes Best Start Family Hubs as a key part of the Government’s wider Best Start in Life strategy, supporting the ambition for more children to achieve a good level of development by age five. The model remains universal and open to families from conception to age 19, or up to 25 for young people with special educational needs and disabilities, while prioritising support for families with babies and young children.
Locally, Worcestershire already has an established Family Hubs offer across the county. This procurement will support the expansion and strengthening of the current model so that it aligns with the additional national expectations for Best Start Family Hubs and Healthy Babies, including improved access, outreach, partnership working and support for families during pregnancy and the early years.
Full details of the requirement can be found in Appendix 1a - Service Specification_Lot 1 and Appendix 1b - Service Specification_Lot 2.
This procurement is split into two Lots:
Lot 1 covers the districts of Bromsgrove, Redditch, Wyre Forest, as well as Great Witley and Tenbury Wells.
Lot 2 covers the districts of Worcester City, Wychavon and Malvern Hills (excluding Great Witley and Tenbury Wells)

criteria.name: Quality criterion 1 (Lot 0)
criteria.description:
Expansion of parenting and HLE interventions in line with national Best Start expectations.
We are seeking a provider that can maximise the reach and impact of parenting support and home learning environment interventions, ensuring more families can access timely, evidence-based support in line with Best Start in Life and Family Hub expectations.
Please describe how you will expand the delivery and uptake of parenting and home learning environment interventions to reach a greater number and wider range of families, in line with national Best Start Family Hub guidance.
Your answer must  include:
• How you will increase awareness and access to parenting and home learning support. 
• How you will reach families who are less likely to engage with services.
• How you will utilise a range of delivery methods, partners and settings to maximise reach. 
• How you will ensure interventions are evidence-based, proportionate to need, and monitored for impact.
• How your approach will result in improved access, reduction in inequalities, increased engagement, and improve parenting/HLE outcomes
• How you will meet and adhere to national requirements, standards and guidance

criteria.name: Quality criterion 2 (Lot 0)
criteria.description:
Outreach and Network Sites
Delivery must ensure Best Start Family Hub services are accessible within local communities and reach families who may be less likely to access support through core Best Start Family Hub buildings.
Please describe how you will develop and deliver a Best Start Family Hub model that extends beyond the core hub sites and into local communities across the contract area.
Your answer must include:
• A practical delivery model for outreach, network sites and access. 
• How you will develop and maintain a network of Best Start Family Hub Network sites.
• A clear proposed model showing how core hubs, outreach, network sites and partner venues will operate together.
• How you will use outreach and community-based delivery to engage families who do not access Family Hub buildings, across the 0–19 age range and with a particular focus on families with children aged 0–5.
• How you will provide effective family navigation by maintaining up-to-date knowledge of local services, building strong links with service providers and VCSE organisations, and enabling families to access the right support through clear in-person and digital routes.
• How you will ensure families experience a smooth and coordinated transition between services for children aged 0–5 and the wider 0–19 offer.
• How you will work with local partners and trusted community organisations to increase reach and accessibility.
(Word count: 1,500 words)

criteria.name: Quality criterion 3 (Lot 0)
criteria.description:

How will you develop and maintain a detailed understanding of the local communities within the area, including local strengths, needs, assets, demographics and inequalities.

• Demonstration of understanding of community strengths, needs and inequalities in local BSFH communities.
• How you will deliver effective engagement with families, communities and local partners. 
• Approaches used to gather family voice and lived experience. Use of this community insight to shape and improve delivery.
• How insight will be translated into service planning and continuous improvement, with examples of how this will be monitored, reviewed and improved
• How you will ensure inclusive access and engagement for vulnerable families, rural communities, families with SEND, and those experiencing digital exclusion.
(Word count: 1,300 words)

criteria.name: Quality criterion 4 (Lot 0)
criteria.description:
Innovation, added value and quality assurance
Providers must demonstrate organisational standards and suitably qualified staff as a key quality assurance measure. We also recognise that providers may be able to bring additional resources, expertise, partnerships and opportunities that enhance Best Start Family Hub delivery and improve outcomes for children, young people and families.
Please describe the innovation, quality assurance and added value your organisation would bring to the delivery of this contract.
Your answer must include:
• How you will implement and maintain quality assurance arrangements, including clear performance indicators and processes for monitoring and improvement.
• How you will recruit, deploy and retain a suitably qualified workforce to manage and deliver services across BSFH and outreach locations, including arrangements to support staff wellbeing.
• How you will draw on the expertise, services and resources within your organisation’s core service offer, alongside the knowledge and expertise available through the wider Best Start network and community services, to strengthen and add value to BSFH delivery.
• Access to additional funding, grants or in-kind resources that would enhance contract delivery.
• How your involvement in national, regional or sector-wide networks and partnerships will add value to local delivery.
• How you will identify, test and embed innovation and best practice, including learning from other areas and services.
• How you will assess and address workforce development, training and skills needs to support high-quality delivery.
(Word count: 1,300 words)

A number of service users within each of the units covered by the service level agreement will have been admitted from outside of the Cheshire footprint and therefore will not be registered with a local GP, or eligible for such registration. tender.title: EU harmonised surveillance of AMR E. coli and Salmonella found in beef and pork
tender.description:
The objective of microbiological food safety research themes is to provide robust information on the presence, growth, survival, and elimination of pathogenic microorganisms throughout the food chain; the extent, distribution, causes, risks and burden of foodborne disease will also be considered where appropriate.  The reduction of foodborne disease has been one of FSA’s key objectives in ensuring food safety. The reduction of foodborne disease is a continuing priority, ensuring that food produced and sold in the UK is safe to eat. We are taking a targeted approach to the control and reduction of individual pathogens, with the aim of reducing the overall burden of foodborne disease in the UK.
The FSA are inviting tenders to carry out a survey of antimicrobial resistant (AMR) E. coli found in fresh beef and pork meat on retail sale in the UK in 2027, in accordance with the Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/1729 and Technical specifications on a randomisation of sampling for the purpose of antimicrobial resistance monitoring from food‐producing animals and food as from 2021. The applicant(s) must be familiar with both the Commission’s Decision and technical specifications to ensure the survey is totally compliant with their specific requirements. 
The survey will be awarded in two procurements:
1. Sampling (This procurement):
Survey design, sample collection at retail and transportation to the testing laboratory
2. Testing (Tendered separately):
Microbiological testing, data analysis, reporting and archiving of recovered bacteria and their AMR profile.
By submitting an application, tenders will be bidding to complete the work required for sampling. Suppliers should note that sampling is operationally dependent upon laboratory testing. The successful sampling supplier will be required to work collaboratively and proactively with the supplier appointed to testing throughout the contract duration. This will include, but not be limited to:
• Agreeing sampling schedules and delivery arrangements.
• Coordinating the transfer of samples to the testing laboratory.
• Sharing sampling data, metadata and supporting documentation.
• Resolving logistical and operational issues to prevent delays to testing activities.
• Participating in joint meetings with the FSA and testing laboratory where required.
The successful sampling supplier will be expected to cooperate fully with the testing laboratory to ensure successful delivery of the overall surveillance programme.

tender.title: DSIT -  Revelio Labs
tender.description:
This procurement is a proportionate, time-limited 12-month data access arrangement designed to meet an urgent evidence need for DSIT/AI Security Institute. The requirement is for access to an existing commercial workforce intelligence dataset, rather than consultancy or bespoke analytical services, and will enable DSIT to test, validate and strengthen the evidence base on AI adoption and labour market impacts. The arrangement is capped at £80,000, with no extension options or open-ended spend commitment, and will be managed within existing programme budgets and governance.
DSIT's AI Security Institute is looking to direct award Revelio Labs for workforce intelligence data to support DSIT's research programme on AI adoption and its impact on the labour market, with a particular focus on skill dynamics, workforce composition, and career trajectories.
Objectives:
1.  Understand how AI adoption reshapes skill demand and supply at the firm level. By acquiring granular, firm-level workforce data (job postings, employee profiles, skill taxonomies, and workforce flows), DSIT's AI & the Future of Work Unit will measure how skill composition evolves at firms actively adopting AI compared to those that are not. 
2.  Provide an empirical benchmark for AI exposure measurement.  Workforce intelligence data enables DSIT to identify which skills actually co-occur with AI adoption at the firm level, providing ground-truth validation of theoretical classifications and improving future measurement frameworks.
3.  Replicate and extend published research on early-career labour market outcomes. To credibly replicate, validate, and extend these estimates for UK policy purposes, DSIT requires access to comparable data of equivalent granularity and structure.
4.  Inform UK workforce and education policy. The evidence generated will directly support policy advice on (examples): which skills retraining programmes should prioritise; where skill gaps are emerging; how curricula should adapt to changing employer expectations; and whether skill dynamics can serve as leading indicators of broader labour market disruption.
5.  Establish early warning capability. By tracking skill shifts that may precede larger employment effects, DSIT aims to build an analytical early warning system that identifies workforce risks before they become visible in aggregate official statistics.
The Arrangement is intended to be entered into by the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology. It is anticipated that the rights and liabilities of the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, including those arising under this Arrangement once executed, will in due course transfer to the Secretary of State for the Cabinet Office pursuant to an Order in Council (secondary legislation) made under section 2 of the Ministers of the Crown Act 1975.

tender.title: Disability Support Service
tender.description:
This is an Invitation to tender for the provision of several support services for The University of Salford Students as outlined in the following lots:
• Lot 1: Educational Psychology assessments to identify specific learning difficulties.
Provision of Educational Psychology assessments to identify and diagnose Specific Learning Difficulties (including dyslexia) for students in a higher education setting, using an evidence based approach (which may include observation, standardised testing and interviews) to identify strengths and support needs.
• Lot 2: Band 1 and 2 non-medical helper support.
Band 1 and 2 support workers assist students with additional needs and disabilities to access and engage with their studies. Support is typically delivered in taught sessions and may include notetaking, practical assistance and support with anxiety management, as appropriate.
• Lot 3: Band 4 non-medical helper support, Specialist Study Skills, and Specialist Mentor support.
One-to-one support delivered outside taught sessions to help students with additional needs to navigate their academic journey. Specialist mentors support students to develop strategies
that promote independence and wellbeing, while specialist study skills tutors help students meet course requirements and build academic confidence.
• Lot 4: Bands 3- 4 non-medical helper support, Specialist D/deaf support.
In-class and out-of-class specialist support to enable d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing students to access and engage with their studies. This may include specialist notetaking, British Sign Language (BSL) interpretation and other specialist support professionals to facilitate communication.
• Lot 5: Bands 1- 4 non-medical helper support, Specialist VI Support for visually impaired students.
In-class and out-of-class specialist support to enable visually impaired students to access and engage with their studies. This may include sighted guide support, mobility training and other
Specialist Support Professionals to support orientation and navigation.
• Lot 6: Band 4 non-medical helper support, Specialist Study Skills and Specialist mentor support for apprentices
One-to-one support delivered outside taught sessions to help apprentices with additional needs to navigate their academic journey, workplace learning and wider apprenticeship requirements. Specialist mentors support apprentices to develop strategies that promote independence and wellbeing, while specialist study skills tutors help apprentices meet course requirements and build academic confidence across academic and workplace settings.
• Lot 7: Neurodiversity screening assessments for apprentices
Neurodiversity screening assessments for apprentices to identify indicators of neurodivergence, including specific learning difficulties and differences in attention, processing and communication, across academic and workplace settings. Assessments should identify strengths, barriers and support needs to inform reasonable adjustments, support planning and, where appropriate, liaison with relevant University and employer contacts.
• Lot 8: Needs assessments for apprenticeship students
Needs assessments for apprenticeship students to identify disability-related support requirements, barriers to participation and adjustments required to support engagement with learning, workplace activity and assessment. Assessments should provide clear recommendations to inform support planning, reasonable adjustments and specialist support across academic and workplace elements of the apprenticeship, including off-the-job training, on-programme learning and end-point assessment, as appropriate.

procedure.features:
This notice is issued in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 to formally announce the initiation of the procurement process. The first stage is now in progress.
Agencies who wish to take part in the process and submit a response should contact emeliawilson@tfl.gov.uk and ensure they are registered on the SAP Ariba e-tendering platform.
Registration is required to receive an invitation to the procurement event and access to the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) documentation.
Agencies intending to submit a response are requested to do so by the deadline of 10:00 AM on 09 September 2027.
The procurement process outlined below is proposed in line with the requirements of the Procurement Act 2023 under the Competitive Flexible Procedure:
Stage 1 : Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ)
The Procurement Specific Questionnaire which contains conditions of participation will allow the GLA  to down select the number of participants invited to the Invitation to tender (ISIT) stage.
Stage 2: ISIT (shortlisting)
The invitation to Submit tender (ISIT) will be issued via our e-tendering portal SAP Ariba and will assess the agencies capabilities in the following areas: Technical ability (Pass / fail and Scored questions), Social Value, Financial and Commercial.
Invitation to Negotiate (ITN) Stage 
TfL may elect to hold one or more negotiation stages following the receipt and the evaluation of the Initial responses. If TfL proceeds to the ITN Stage, it may conduct negotiations with some or all of the Bidders that submitted compliant Initial Offers and satisfied the Technical Submission requirements as detailed in this ISIT. The objective of these negotiations is to allow Bidders to improve the content of their Initial Offers and further develop their solution for delivering the contract. 
ITSFT- Negotiation/ BAFO (Optional)
If TfL decide to proceed to a negotiation stage after receipt and evaluation of Initial financial submission, bidders will be requested to resubmit the overall sum pricing as part of a BAFO submission which must not exceed the price submitted in the original submission or a bid will be automatically disqualified.
